national_raw_news.title: 19 mins ago | National 110 Nation observes Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
national_raw_news.content: Today is Partition Horrors Remembrance Day. The nation is paying homage to all of those who sacrificed their lives and suffered unimaginable pain during the partition in 1947. Akashvani correspondent reports that, on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, various programmes are being organised across the country, including in the National Capital. In a fitting tribute to all those who lost their lives due to the partition of the nation and were displaced from their roots, in 2021, the Government had decided to observe 14th August every year as the day to commemorate their sacrifice. It also ensures that future generations remember the pain and suffering endured by the people, as the birth of independent India was marked by the violent partition, which left lasting scars on millions. The Partition Horrors Remembrance Day keeps reminding people of the need to remove the poison of social divisions and disharmony and further strengthen the spirit of oneness, social harmony and human empowerment. The partition caused one of the largest migrations in human history, affecting about 20 million people. While celebrating independence, a grateful nation also salutes those people who had to sacrifice their lives in the frenzy of violence.

national_raw_news.title: 37 mins ago | Sports 25 Iga Swiatek beats Elena Rybakina to claim Women’s Singles title at Canadian Open Tennis
national_raw_news.content: In Canadian Open Tennis, seventh seed Iga Swiatek of Poland defeated second seed Elena Rybakina in straight sets to claim the Women’s Singles title in Toronto last night. Swiatek captured her first title of the season with a swift 6-2 6-3 win, giving her a confidence boost heading into the US Open. In Men’s Singles, American tennis player Ben Shelton won the title in Montreal by defeating fellow American Brandon Nakashima with a score of 6-3, 7-6(4). With this victory, the fifth-seeded Shelton successfully defended his tournament crown and captured his second career ATP Masters 1000 trophy. This victory marks his fourth tournament win of the 2026 season, following earlier titles in Dallas, Munich, and Stuttgart, bringing his total career tour-level titles to seven.

national_raw_news.title: PoJK protest becomes global
national_raw_news.content: The unrest in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK) has taken an international turn through protests by the Kashmiri diaspora to expose state-sponsored terror by the Pakistani establishment. In Belgium, Kashmiri diaspora groups today marched from the European Parliament toward the United Nations in Brussels, calling for international scrutiny of the situation in PoJK. In Italy, large diaspora demonstrations were reported in Bologna, condemning deaths and alleged abuses by Pakistani security forces and expressing support for the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). In UK, protests have also taken place outside Pakistani diplomatic premises, with Britain based Kashmiris highlighting alleged human-rights violations in PoJK. Earlier, the Awami Action Committee had called on Kashmiris worldwide to hold demonstrations today to draw international attention to the atrocities committed by the Pakistani establishment in the region. Meanwhile, the situation in PoJK remains tense, with protesters raising questions about recent controversial elections conducted under the influence of Pakistani force, targetted killings and forced disappearances of innocent people and supply disruptions. Jammu and Kashmir Joint Action Committee (JKJAAC) senior leader Sardar Shabir has claimed that around 100 people had been killed by Pakistani forces during the unrest in the occupied territory. Protests in PoJK have continued for more than two months, with demonstrators raising various demands.

national_raw_news.title: UNSC links Delhi Red Fort suicide car bombing to Al-Qaida in Indian Subcontinent
national_raw_news.content: A terrorism monitoring team of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has declared the deadly Red Fort suicide car bombing in Delhi that killed 11 people the work of Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS). The report by the Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team on terrorism to the Security Council said, the attack in last November was officially attributed to AQIS. The report said, AQIS continued to evolve from a fragmented group into a regional terrorist entity and it established logistics and financial networks, working in decentralised small, scattered cells instead of large units. It was also highlighted in the report that AQIS is trying to exploit Bangladesh to establish cells there. Against this backdrop, the team warned that terrorist threats intensified in South Asia. AQIS was founded in 2014 by Al-Qaida leader Ayman al-Zawahiri. Based in New York, Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team comprises ten experts who track global terrorism threats from those groups and their affiliates and provide periodic reports and updates to help the committees decide on groups and individuals to be sanctioned for terror related activities. An earlier report by the team released in February said Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) was reported to be linked to an attack on the Red Fort, and the new report appears to directly pin the blame on AQIS. According to the Committee, JeM has had close ties with Al-Qaida.

national_raw_news.title: Iran refutes President Trump’s claim of seizing Strait of Hormuz
national_raw_news.content: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi today rejected US President Donald Trump’s claim that Washington has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. In a social media post, Mr. Araghchi accused the US of repeatedly making miscalculations over the strategic waterway due to intelligence failures. The remarks came after Mr Trump claimed that the United States has total control over the Strait of Hormuz and would retain it. He also claimed that Iran’s military infrastructure had been severely degraded. Iran has rejected Mr. Trump claims, saying that the strategic waterway remains blocked and will not be reopened until Tehran’s conditions are accepted.

national_raw_news.title: Commonwealth Fencing: Indian team dominates with 35 medals comprising 13 gold 13 Aug 2026 | 8:30 PM 721
national_raw_news.content: India emerged as the overall champions at the Commonwealth Fencing Championship by winning an impressive 35 medals after four days of competition held at Lagos in Nigeria. Indian contingent secured thirteen gold, eight silver, and fourteen bronze medals at the event across the Under 23 and senior competitions. The senior Indian fencers claimed five gold medals in six events on the fourth and final day of the competition, securing honours in Men’s Sabre, Women’s Sabre, Men’s E’pée, Women’s Epée and Women’s foil, as well as a silver in Men’s foil. The performance also helped India win the Wilkinson Sword Trophy, awarded by the Commonwealth Fencing Federation to the country with the best overall results. Secretary-general, Fencing Association of India, Rajeev Mehta, said in a statement that lifting the Commonwealth Overall Championship title for the first time is a testament to the talent, discipline, and hard work within Indian fencing.

national_raw_news.title: Country’s exports register robust growth of over 13% in July 13 Aug 2026 | 8:45 PM 145
national_raw_news.content: The country’s total exports, including merchandise and services are estimated at 80.14 billion US dollars in July this year, registering a robust 13.3 per cent year-on-year growth. According to the provisional data released by the Commerce Ministry, the export performance was led by merchandise shipments, which jumped over 19.6 per cent to 44.24 billion US dollars from a year earlier. The growth in merchandise exports was driven by petroleum products, electronic goods, engineering goods, organic and inorganic chemicals, cotton yarn and handloom products. Country’s merchandise trade deficit widened by 31.5 per cent year-on-year to 15 billion US dollars last month. Cumulatively, merchandise exports during April to July period of the current financial year are estimated at 173.78 billion US dollars, registering an increase of 17 per cent on an annual basis.

national_raw_news.title: NITI Aayog highlights 12 priority sectors to make India a global manufacturing hub 13 Aug 2026 | 5:40 PM 133
national_raw_news.content: Vice Chairperson of NITI Aayog, Ashok Kumar Lahiri today released a report titled Key Sectors to Position India as a Global Manufacturing Hub. It also lays down a strategic roadmap to strengthen India’s manufacturing ecosystem and support the vision of Viksit Bharat. Addressing the occasion, Dr Lahiri emphasized that manufacturing must play a significantly larger role to fulfill India’s long-term growth aspirations. (DC) As Preferred Source Hyderabad: Organ donation needs to be brought into public conversation and families and communities should be encouraged to discuss it to bridge the gap between the demand for organs and their availability, said Dr Sree Bhushan Raju, professor and head of nephrology at the Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (Nims). While medical science has advanced in transplantation procedures and medicines, he said the availability of organs ultimately determines how many patients awaiting transplantation can receive treatment, he said. Dr Raju, heads of the State Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisation (SOTTO), was seaking at a workshop, ‘Myths and Facts on Organ Donation’, organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), here to mark World Organ Donation Day. Explaining transplantation, Dr Raju said the immune system would naturally recognize a transplanted organ as foreign and attempt to reject it. Medicines can control this response, but doctors have to maintain a balance between preventing rejection and protecting recipients from infections. He also highlighted swap transplantation as an option for patients whose willing family donors are medically incompatible. Under the appropriate legal and medical framework, compatible donor-recipient pairs can be matched for transplantation. Opening the workshop, Dr Manas Krishnakanth, joint director, PIB-Hyderabad, said there was a significant gap between the demand for organ transplants and the availability of donor organs in the country. Speaking on the occasion, the President said that the performing artists honoured today collectively present a cultural map of India--a map woven with stories and songs native to this soil; a map that encompasses the dances and festivals of this diverse land and holds the memories of its languages and dialects, shaped over centuries. She was happy to note that the Sangeet Natak Akademi is organising the 'Kala-Diksha' program with this very objective. She urged senior artists to make systematic efforts to groom the next generation. Acclaimed ghazal singer and composer Ustad Yugantar Sindoor, senior Kathak maestro Pandit Rammohan Maharaj of the Kalka-Bindadin Gharana, and veteran photographer Rakesh Sinha were among the distinguished artists felicitated at the ceremony. national_raw_news.content: PIB Backgrounder India’s Energy Journey: Expanding Capacity, Strengthening Security Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 3:30PM by PIB Delhi India’s Energy Landscape India’s energy landscape is evolving to meet rising demand while strengthening energy security and supporting a cleaner future. The transformation spans renewable energy, nuclear power, petroleum, natural gas, coal and emerging technologies. Policy support, infrastructure development, domestic production, manufacturing expansion and wider energy access are shaping this transformation. India is simultaneously expanding non-fossil energy capacity, strengthening domestic energy resources and developing new technologies for the future. Numbers At a Glance: Total installed power capacity: Around 552 GW in July 2026, up from 249 GW in 2014. Non-fossil capacity: 300.50 GW as of 31 July 2026, accounting for over 54% of total installed capacity. India ranks third globally in renewable energy installed capacity. It meets nearly 55 per cent of the country’s primary energy needs and supports over 70 per cent of its electricity generation . Experts stressed the importance of donor families, public awareness and voluntary pledges, while NOTTO’s Jug Jug Jiyo campaign seeks to encourage organ donation. By Telangana Today Published Date - 13 August 2026, 08:45 PM PIB Hyderabad organizes Varta, media workshop on World Organ Donation Day Hyderabad: The Press Information Bureau (PIB) Hyderabad organized Varta, a media workshop on the theme Myths and Facts on Organ Donation, on the occasion of World Organ Donation Day at CGO Towers, Kavadiguda. In his address, Dr. Sree Bhushan Raju, Professor and Head of the Department of Nephrology and Head of SOTTO (Jeevandan) at Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), said, “On World Organ Donation Day, we must recognize organ donation as a noble act through which a deceased person can give another person a new lease of life. While medical science has made remarkable advances in transplantation, human organs cannot yet be fully replicated, making the generosity of donors and their families invaluable.” Explaining the complexities involved in transplantation, he mentioned the human immune system naturally recognized a transplanted organ as a foreign substance and attempts to reject it. To prevent this, advances in medicine have made it possible to control this immune response and enhance the outcomes of transplantation. Dr. Manas Krishnakanth, IIS, Joint Director of PIB Hyderabad, said, “Through the media workshops like Varta, we provide informative sessions on debunking myths or misconceptions surrounding organ donation and distinguish them from medical facts.” On Indian Organ Donation Day, the National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organization (NOTTO) has launched the “Jug Jug Jiyo (Angdaan Karo, Jug Jug Jiyo)” movement to inspire voluntary family discussions and pledges. These efforts aim to create greater public awareness, encourage organ donation, and strengthen the transplantation ecosystem across the country. A 24×7 toll-free helpline at 1800-11-477 is also available to provide information and assistance related to organ donation. national_raw_news.content: NITI Aayog NITI Aayog Report on “Key Sectors to Position India as a Global Manufacturing Hub” Strengthening India’s Manufacturing Aspirations: Major Sectors to drive India’s growth story Key Sectors to Position India as a Global Manufacturing Hub: Strategic Importance, Value Chain Play and Operational Efficiency Advancing the Vision of Viksit Bharat through effective interventions for furthering Manufacturing Ecosystem Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 4:56PM by PIB Delhi NITI Aayog has released the report titled “ Key Sectors to Position India as a Global Manufacturing Hub ”, which through a structured and data-driven framework identifies major sectors that can fuel India’s ambition to become global manufacturing powerhouse. This report has extensively analyzed four sectors viz. Chemicals, Telecom & Networking Equipments, Textiles and Solar Photo Voltaic manufacturing. The assessment focuses on understanding India’s manufacturing landscape in relation to global trends, sectoral growth opportunities and global benchmarks. It also examines the factors that influence manufacturing competitiveness, including market potential, infrastructure readiness, policy support, raw material availability, technology readiness, employment potential and India’s current position in the value chain. The project seeks to identify sectors where India has significant growth potential and where targeted interventions can strengthen domestic capabilities, enhance competitiveness and value addition, and accelerate export-oriented manufacturing growth. The study also draws on the experience of leading manufacturing countries to develop sector-specific recommendations for addressing key challenges and promoting growth in the identified sectors. The study was structured into four distinct phases: Phase 1: Shortlisting Sectors Based on Relative Attractiveness: Identification of sectors with high growth potential based on market size and growth prospects in both domestic and global markets. Phase 2: Comprehensive Assessment of Shortlisted Sectors: A detailed, three-pronged assessment of the shortlisted sectors to evaluate their market potential, competitiveness, and broader strategic relevance. Phase 3: Benchmarking International Best Practices: Analyses of best practices and successful approaches adopted by top performing countries to identify relevant strategies and lessons for India’s shortlisted sectors. Phase 4: Developing Actionable Recommendations and the Way Forward: Formulation of sector-specific, actionable recommendations and a clear roadmap to strengthen competitiveness, unlock growth potential, and position India as a global manufacturing hub. This edition of the report focuses on four high-potential manufacturing sectors: chemicals, textiles, telecom and network equipment and solar photovoltaic manufacturing. This will be followed by reports on 8 more sectors. national_raw_news.content: PIB Backgrounder Building a Business-Ready India Advancing Ease of Doing Business, Empowering Enterprises Posted On: 13 AUG 2026 5:01PM by PIB Delhi Enabling Enterprise-Led Growth As India celebrates its 80th Independence Day, the nation continues to strengthen the foundations of a self-reliant, resilient and growing economy. The Government has undertaken reforms aimed at reducing compliance burdens, enhancing transparency, encouraging entrepreneurship and creating greater opportunities for enterprises of all sizes. These efforts are advancing Ease of Doing Business through digital single-window systems, simplified incorporation processes, wider market access, improved access to finance and trust-based regulation. Reforming India’s Business Environment From digital single-window clearances to large-scale regulatory clean-ups, the focus of the reforms is on creating a predictable and facilitation-driven business environment. National Single Window System (NSWS): It is a single window digital platform which guides in identifying and applying for approvals according to the business requirements. The system integrates approvals across 32 Central ministries and 34 States . It provides access to over 686 central and 7,498 state approvals. Since its launch in 2021, NSWS has granted over 8.29 lakh approvals (November, 2025). Startup India (2016): The initiative aims to support entrepreneurs and build a robust startup ecosystem. It seeks to transform India into a nation of job creators rather than job seekers. DPIIT-recognised startups increased from 502 in 2016 to over 2.47 lakh as on 12 August 2026 . SPICe+ Form (2020): This web-based form integrates 11 services from 3 Central Government ministries and departments . The form integrates 10 essential procedures including name reservation, incorporation, DIN allotment, PAN issuance, TAN issuance, EPFO registration, ESIC registration, Profession Tax registration, Bank account opening, and GSTIN allotment, and First-Time Registration of Shops and Establishment for all new companies getting incorporated in Delhi. It thereby, reduces procedural burden, saves time and lowers compliance costs for businesses. MCA21 V3: MCA21 Project , a forward-looking, AI-driven initiative significantly enhances transparency in India’s corporate landscape. The platform is used for end-to-end registry and incorporation related services of companies & limited liability partnerships (LLPs) . Between 2021 and 2025, it processed 3.84 crore filings , with 3.33 crore approved through Straight Through Process. Udyam Registration (2020): It offers a free, paperless, and self-declaration-based system for MSMEs (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises). MSME registrations on the Udyam Portal increased from 0.10 lakh in October 2020 to over 9.27 lakh b y 13 th August 2026. Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) : Launched in 2015, BRAP promotes Ease of Doing Business by simplifying regulations and improving transparency across States and Union Territories (UTs). It covers reforms across single-window clearances, land, labour, inspections, taxation, environmental approvals and others. Unlocking Finance for Enterprise Growth Credit guarantees, digital lending and receivables financing are widening access to formal finance, particularly for MSMEs.
